# Quick Start

Purpose: get from first launch to your first retirement simulation in about ten minutes.

## What you need

- **iPhone:** iOS 27 or later. The iPhone version is distributed through TestFlight first.
- **Mac:** a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later. See [MAC_INSTALLATION.md](MAC_INSTALLATION.md).
- Rough figures: your age, planned retirement age, yearly spending, expected Social Security, and the balances of your accounts.
- Optional: Wi-Fi and 2 to 8 GB of free space, only if you want to download an AI model (see step 5). You can also use a model server you already run.

Longstead works without an account and without an internet connection. Everything you enter stays on your device.

## 1. Complete the setup wizard

The first time you open the app (iPhone, iPad or Mac), a six-step wizard appears. A progress dot row at the top shows where you are. Use the back arrow to return to an earlier step. It takes about two minutes, and you can change everything later in **Profile**.

1. **Welcome.** Read the intro and tap **Continue**. A line below the button says that continuing means you agree to the Terms of Use and acknowledge the Privacy Policy and AI Disclaimer, with links to each.
2. **Who you are.** Enter your name, choose your filing status (Single, Married filing jointly, Married filing separately, Head of household, or Qualifying widow(er)), and enter your state.
   - Choose your state from the picker (all 50 states and DC). It is stored as a two-letter code. State income tax tables are bundled for CA, NY, IL, PA, TX, FL, WA, NV and NJ, and states with no income tax (AK, FL, NV, NH, SD, TN, TX, WA, WY) count as zero. For any other state the app warns that state tables are not included yet and shows federal tax only.
3. **Your timeline.** Use the steppers for current age (18 to 100), retire at (30 to 95), plan through (60 to 110), and claim Social Security at (62 to 70). The app keeps the order consistent for you: current age < retire at < plan through.
4. **Your spending.** Enter your yearly spending in retirement in today's dollars. Enter your expected monthly Social Security. If you chose Married filing jointly, a field for your spouse's monthly benefit also appears.
   - Enter the monthly benefit **at the age you plan to claim**. The simulation uses the number exactly as entered from your claim age onward and does not adjust it for claiming early or late.
5. **Risk tolerance.** Pick Conservative, Balanced, or Growth. It is saved to your profile (as Conservative, Moderate or Aggressive) and sets the starting real return and volatility on the Simulate screen: 3% and 8%, 5% and 12%, or 7% and 16%. You can still change them with sliders.
6. **Review.** Check the summary and tap **Start planning**.

If **Continue** is greyed out, a message above the button says what to fix (for example, "Add your name to continue.").

The wizard appears the first time you open the app. You can change any answer later in **Profile**.

## 2. Add your accounts

1. Open the **Accounts** tab and tap **+** (or **Add account**).
2. Enter a name and choose the account **Type**. The **Tax treatment** fills in from the type (401(k), 403(b), 457(b), IRAs, pension and annuity: Tax-Deferred; Roth accounts: Tax-Free; HSA: Tax-Exempt; brokerage, savings, CD, ESPP, RSU, real estate and other: Taxable) until you pick one yourself. Check it, especially for unusual accounts.
3. Enter the balance, the annual contribution, and any employer match. Contributions and match stop when you reach your retirement age.
4. Tap **Save**. Repeat for each account.

## 3. Run your first simulation

1. Open the **Simulate** tab. A 10,000-path simulation runs automatically.
2. Tap **Run 10,000 paths** for the full result.
3. Read **Plan health**: the share of simulated futures in which your money lasts to your "plan through" age. Green is 80% or more, amber is 60 to 79%, red is below 60%.
4. Drag the sliders under **Assumptions** (real return, volatility, retirement age, horizon) to see how the result changes. The preview refreshes as you drag.

## 4. Look at the withdrawal plan

Open the **Withdraw** tab to see which accounts the plan draws from in each phase: Bridge, Pre-RMD, RMD, and Late. It needs a profile and at least one account.

## 5. Set up AI chat (Council tab)

The **Council** tab holds your AI advisors. There are three ways they can run:

- **Apple's built-in on-device model (Apple Intelligence).** This is the default. If your device supports it and it is switched on in iOS Settings, you do not have to download anything. Open **Council**, tap an advisor, and ask a question.
- **A downloaded open-source model.** If Apple Intelligence is not available, or you prefer an open model:
  1. Tap the gear icon at the top right of the **Plan** tab to open **Settings**.
  2. Tap **Manage models**.
  3. Tap **Download** next to the model marked **recommended** for your device. It is a one-time download from huggingface.co. Use Wi-Fi.
  4. When the row shows **Installed**, return to **Council** and start a chat.
- **Your own model server (Ollama, LM Studio or another).** If you already run one, the app can use it.

**Automatic Ollama setup.** The first time you open a chat, the app looks for Ollama on your computer (at `http://localhost:11434`). If Ollama is running, the app connects, picks a good model for each advisor and shows a notice in the chat header with **Change models** and **Use Apple's built-in model instead**. If Ollama is installed on your Mac but not running, the header offers **Open Ollama**. If Ollama is not found, the header says chat uses Apple's built-in model by default and offers to install Ollama, to download a capable model directly (recommended for your device), or to keep Apple's model. Nothing is downloaded or switched without you seeing it. See [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

If a chat shows "Download a model to chat", the advisor has no model to use; the button takes you to the same download screen.

Details on choosing a model are in [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

## 6. Ask your first question

In **Council**, open **Tax Consultant** and try: "I am single, 58 years old, in CA, with $90,000 of income in 2026. What is my total tax?" Include the year, your filing status, your state, and the amounts in every question, because the advisor remembers only your last two exchanges in a chat.

For your own plan numbers, open the **Retirement Planner** and tap **My plan numbers (no AI)**. It posts the planning engine's figures instantly with no model involved, labelled "Planning engine (no AI)". If a required input is missing (current age, retirement age, yearly spending, filing status, or savings in at least one account), it tells you which one.
